name: Tesla Megapack in AI data centers: what it is, what it does, and how xAI uses it
title: Tesla Megapack in AI data centers: what it is, what it does, and how xAI uses it
answer: A Tesla Megapack is a shipping container sized lithium iron phosphate battery built for utility scale storage. At an AI data center it does three jobs the grid alone cannot: it carries the load through outages and surges, it shaves the peaks a training run puts on the utility, and it lets a campus start drawing power before the grid connection is fully ready. xAI is the largest known user, with hundreds of units at its Colossus sites in Memphis and Southaven, Mississippi.

sources.title: xAI has quietly built a massive battery at its Memphis data center hub (Canary Media)
xAI deploys 168 Tesla Megapacks at Colossus (DatacenterDynamics)

sections.body: Each Megapack is a factory built enclosure holding battery modules, an inverter, thermal management and fire protection, delivered ready to connect. The Megapack 2 XL that most current sites use stores about 3.9 megawatt hours. The Megapack 3, announced at RE+ in September 2025, raises that to about 5 megawatt hours per unit using larger 2.8 litre lithium iron phosphate cells, and Tesla says it needs 78 percent fewer internal connections thanks to a simpler thermal bay. Tesla also introduced the Megablock: four Megapack 3 units prewired to a medium voltage transformer and switchgear, about 20 megawatt hours per block, which Tesla says cuts installation time by 23 percent and construction cost by 40 percent and packs about 248 megawatt hours onto an acre. Tesla rates the Megablock for a 25 year life, more than 10,000 cycles, 91 percent round trip efficiency and operation from minus 40 to 60 degrees Celsius.
sections.heading: What a Megapack is

sections.body: Megapack 3 and Megablock are built at Tesla's Megafactory in Brookshire, Texas, west of Houston, planned for 50 gigawatt hours a year, roughly 10,000 Megapack 3 units. Tesla originally targeted production for late 2026; Canary Media reported that Megapack 3 production began in early August 2026, ahead of that plan. Earlier generations come from Tesla's Lathrop, California and Shanghai factories.
sections.heading: Where they are made

sections.body: Training clusters draw power in sharp swings as thousands of GPUs start and stop together, which utilities find hard to serve. A battery sits between the grid and the load and evens those swings out, so the utility sees a steadier draw. It also rides through the seconds or minutes when a generator trips or the grid sags, protecting a training run that could otherwise lose hours of work, and it can supply the peaks a campus needs during periods when the grid is already strained. What it cannot do is replace a power plant: a battery holds hours of energy, not days, so it works alongside gas generation or a grid connection, not instead of them.
sections.heading: What a battery does at an AI data center

sections.body: At Colossus 1, the former Electrolux plant on Paul Lowry Road in Memphis, xAI installed 168 Megapacks by May 2025, which the Greater Memphis Chamber said provide about 150 megawatts to ride through outages and demand surges; the site was also connected to a new 150 megawatt substation. A later satellite count by Cleanview found 119 Megapacks in three clusters, about 120 megawatts. Tesla reported selling xAI roughly 230 million dollars of Megapacks between January 2024 and February 2025, and 430 million dollars in 2025 in a January 2026 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. At Colossus 2, Canary Media counted 720 Megapacks in satellite imagery dated 11 July 2026, which an xAI energy developer described to the Tennessee Valley Authority board as the biggest battery in the nation and a precondition for connecting service. If those units are 3.9 megawatt hour Megapack 2 XLs, that is on the order of 2.8 gigawatt hours, an estimate by this site, not a published figure.
sections.heading: How xAI uses Megapacks

sections.body: Three questions decide how far this model spreads. First, duration: batteries cover peaks and outages, so a campus still needs firm generation, which at xAI has meant gas turbines and a dedicated plant site in Southaven. Second, related parties: xAI, now part of SpaceX, buying hundreds of millions of dollars of storage from Tesla, another Elon Musk company, is a commercial relationship worth tracking in both companies' filings. Third, whether Megablock's faster installation makes batteries a standard first step for any large AI campus waiting on a grid connection.
